c.tagline: A perfectly preserved medieval old town on the Danube, sausages and all

taxi.fareNote: Taxis are metered and reliable but pricier than public transit; ranks are found at the train station and Old Town squares.

emergency.note: 112 reaches both fire and ambulance services anywhere in Germany; 110 is the general police line.

english.label: Easy to get by in English

hood_landmark.Stadtamhof: Northern end of the Stone Bridge

hood_desc: The UNESCO-listed medieval core, packed with Gothic towers, the Stone Bridge, the cathedral, and the Wurstkuchl sausage kitchen; nearly car-free and best explored on foot.
A small, quiet quarter just across the Danube from the Altstadt, with its own village-like main street, church, and river views back toward the old town.
An up-and-coming riverside district east of the center with parks, indie bars, and a younger, more relaxed vibe than the historic core.
A residential district south of the center with Roman-era remains, local bakeries, and everyday German neighborhood life away from the tourist crowds.
Home to the University of Regensburg campus, with student bars, budget eats, and a livelier nightlife scene than the historic center.

water.note: Tap water is safe and of high quality.

transit.hours: roughly 4:30am-1am, with limited night buses on weekends
transit.pay: RVV tickets via app, machines, or onboard; day passes available
transit.note: Regensburg is famously the largest German city without a tram network; buses cover the whole city well and the Altstadt is walkable end to end.

train: Regensburg Hauptbahnhof has frequent ICE/regional connections to Munich, Nuremberg, and Frankfurt
bus: FlixBus connects Regensburg to major German cities

tip.r: Round up the bill or add roughly 5-10%, handed directly to the server rather than left on the table.

landmarks: Steinerne Brücke (Stone Bridge)
A 12th-century engineering marvel spanning the Danube on sixteen arches, the medieval crossing that made Regensburg rich and inspired bridges across Europe.
Regensburg Cathedral (Dom St. Peter)
Bavaria's finest Gothic cathedral, its lacy twin spires soaring above the old town and its choir home to the famous Domspatzen boys' choir.
Altes Rathaus (Old Town Hall)
The Gothic seat of the Perpetual Imperial Diet from 1663 to 1806, where guided tours visit the Reichssaal and original torture chambers.
Historische Wurstkuchl
Reputedly the world's oldest sausage kitchen, grilling bratwurst beside the Danube for 850 years, since the stone bridge's builders needed lunch.
Porta Praetoria
A rugged stone gate from the Roman legionary fortress of Castra Regina, built in 179 AD and still embedded in the city's fabric.
Schloss Thurn und Taxis (St. Emmeram Palace)
One of Europe's largest inhabited palaces, where the postal-dynasty princes converted a great Benedictine abbey into staterooms of jaw-dropping opulence.
Basilika St. Emmeram
A thousand-year-old abbey church transformed by the Asam brothers into a Baroque vision of frescoes, gilt and saintly tombs.
Haidplatz
A theatrically beautiful triangular square of patrician towers and the medieval Goldenes Kreuz inn, where emperors lodged and tournaments were fought.
Schottenkirche St. Jakob
A 12th-century Romanesque monastery church founded by Irish monks, famed for its enigmatic sculpture-crowded north portal, the Schottenportal.
Walhalla
A gleaming Parthenon replica above the Danube east of the city, built by King Ludwig I to enshrine marble busts of German greats.

train.note: No direct international trains - for Prague or Vienna you change at Nuremberg, Munich or Plzeň. Regensburg Hbf has fast regional and IC services to Munich in about 90 minutes, Nuremberg in an hour and Passau on the Danube. The station is a ten-minute walk from the old town. DB Sparpreis fares open six months ahead.

bus.note: The Prague coach is genuinely useful here - it runs direct in about four hours and is faster than the rail alternative, which needs two changes. Coaches use the stop at the Hauptbahnhof. Carry your passport or EU ID card even though this is an internal Schengen crossing.

ferry.note: There is no scheduled passenger ferry. Regensburg is a major Danube river-cruise port and day boats run downstream to the Walhalla monument in summer, but these are excursions rather than scheduled transport. A small ferry crosses to Stadtamhof.

half.name: Weltenburg Abbey
half.blurb: A Benedictine monastery about 45 minutes away brews beer and sits at the mouth of the Danube gorge, reachable also by boat through the cliffs.

half.name: Kelheim
half.blurb: A town about 30 minutes southwest holds the Befreiungshalle, a domed 19th-century monument to the wars against Napoleon.

half.name: Straubing
half.blurb: A Danube city about 40 minutes east hosts the Gäubodenvolksfest and keeps its Gothic city tower and a late-medieval gate.

half.name: Passau
half.blurb: A city about an hour away sits at the confluence of three rivers and has a Baroque cathedral with a large church organ.
